collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The warriors leave to guard the far beach for a moon: give them a feast, or send them with food for the journey.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The warriors are leaving to guard the far beach for a whole moon, where the raiders landed last year. (subject) is going with them. (friend) wants to give them a feast tonight, with songs. (subject) thinks the village should save its food and pack it for the warriors instead. What should the village do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village feasts the warriors, and every family brings something. The songs go on late. (subject) leaves at dawn with a full belly, a bad head and a bag of dried fish from (friend). (subject.He/she) says it was worth it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village packs the food: dried fish, breadfruit, coconut. (friend) sings a short song at the edge of the village as the warriors leave, and everyone joins in. It is not a feast. But out on the far beach, the warriors eat well for the whole moon.
